process_steps.input_state: CP-Ti powder coated with naphthenic oil

evidence.quote: the CP-Ti powder was coated with 0.02 wt% naphthenic oil (Clesafe oil H8, JXTG Nippon Oil & Energy Co.) to enhance adhesion of the alloying particles using a tabletop ball mill (AV-2, Asahi Rika Seisakusho) at 90 rpm for 1 h.

process_steps.input_state: coated CP-Ti powder, Fe particles, deoxygenated Re particles

evidence.quote: Subsequently, the coated CP-Ti powder, as-received Fe particles and deoxygenated Re particles were mixed with 10 wt% media balls with a diameter of 10 mm using a rock milling (RM-05, Seiwa Giken Co.) for 3 h with a frequency of 60 Hz

The mixed feedstock powders were consolidated by spark plasma sintering (SPS, SPS-1030S, SPS Syntech Co.). The feedstock was filled into a carbon container with an inner diameter of 36 mm, and then heated to 1000 ℃ at a rate of 20 ℃ /min. The temperature was held for 1 h under vacuum (6 Pa) with a uniaxial pressure of 30 MPa.
The sintered sample was then subjected to a solution treatment (ST) at 1450 ℃ for 1 h followed by water quenching, aiming to dissolve Re homogeneously in the Ti – Fe matrix.

Finally, the solution-treated sample was hot-extruded to obtain a fully dense specimen using a 2000 kN hydraulic press (SHP-200 – 450, Shibayama Machine Co.). Preheating was performed at 850 ◦ C for 300 s in an argon atmosphere at a heating rate of 2 ◦ C/s using an infrared gold image furnace (RHL-P610C, Advance Riko, Inc.). The extrusion was conducted with a punch speed of 6 mm/s and an extrusion ratio of 18.5 (container diameter: 37 mm, die diameter: 10 mm).

attributes.morphology: globular α grains in a β matrix aligned and partially connected to ED

evidence.quote: Ti-4Fe exhibited globular α grains in a β matrix aligned and partially connected to ED, which were developed through grain deformation and continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) during hot extrusion
The β phase area fraction proportionally increased from 19.7 % (Ti-4Fe) to 76.1 % (Ti-4Fe-4.0Re) at the increment of 14 % per 1 wt% Re, clearly demonstrating the β -stabilizing effect of Re.

attributes.morphology: intragranular acicular α phase and intergranular grain boundary α phase (αGB)

evidence.quote: the high Re content, i.e., 1.5 ~ 4.0 %Re, distinctly led to the formation of an intragranular acicular α phase and an intergranular grain boundary α phase ( α GB ) ( Fig. 3 (c) – (e)), which are typical morphologies of transformed α phases in α + β Ti alloys extruded above the β transus temperature
The β phase area fraction proportionally increased from 19.7 % (Ti-4Fe) to 76.1 % (Ti-4Fe-4.0Re) at the increment of 14 % per 1 wt% Re, clearly demonstrating the β -stabilizing effect of Re.
